clue.text: Even I'd thrown out a bit of salad!

indicators.note: letters thrown out of order are rearranged, so the clue's opening words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone protests indignantly that even their contribution of greenery was binned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' looks like rejection of the salad but signals the anagram of EVENID.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a bitter leafy plant eaten raw as a salad leaf.

clue.text: Most senior English lord is in Paris

parts.note: est is French for is

explanation.surface: The oldest English aristocrat is living in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest is the oldest, the one highest in age among siblings.

clue.text: Revolutionary list observed — it could be explosive

indicators.note: something turning in revolution is read the other way round

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
noted means observed

explanation.surface: A radical's roll of names has been spotted, possibly with a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the device that sets off a charge, so it is part of what blows up.

clue.text: Composer seen in very small supermarket after six

indicators.note: the very small supermarket comes after the six

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
Aldi is a budget supermarket chain with compact stores

explanation.surface: A famous musician spotted in a little grocery shop just after six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was the Venetian Baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: One anticipating a match being planned?

definitions.meaning: the person one is engaged to marry, looking forward to the match
... as an adjective means planned or meant

explanation.definitionFit: An intended is a fiancé or fiancée awaiting the wedding; as an adjective the word means designed or purposed.

clue.text: My heavenly body's collapsed — at rest on run going wrong

indicators.note: the words go wrong, ending up in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone laments their body gave way, resting after a botched jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation; 'heavenly body' looks like vanity about a physique.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron star is the extremely dense remnant left when a massive star implodes.

clue.text: Wind round hospital department taking drink

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A ward staff gets sozzled with alcohol, swirling round.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or wrap something around another thing.

clue.text: Pet outside home is performing

indicators.note: the pet goes round the word for home

parts.note: a dog is a pet
in means at home

explanation.surface: A dog outside the house is putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing means carrying out or performing an action.

clue.text: Entertainers undress naughtily, enthralling front of audience

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the jumbled letters hold another inside
naughtily suggests the letters misbehave and get out of order
takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Performers strip cheekily, captivating the front row.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of UNDRESS, from 'naughtily', gives DNSEURS; 'enthralling' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Danseurs are male ballet dancers, performers who entertain on stage.

clue.text: Case of inhabitant wanting new leader

indicators.note: the word for inhabitant needs its first letter swapped for a different one

parts.note: a native is someone born in and living in a place

explanation.surface: A file about a resident who needs a fresh boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting new leader' says NATIVE's first letter is replaced; the replacement D is left for the definition to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case, marking the indirect object in languages such as Latin and German.

clue.text: European or American gangster shunned by someone down under

indicators.note: the gangster is avoided by, so dropped out of, the Australian

parts.note: down under is slang for Australia, so this is an Australian
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives AL

explanation.surface: A choice between a European and a mobster whom an Australian cold-shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: An Austrian comes from Austria, a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Bloomer in newspaper with female getting humble

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to humble someone is to lower them

explanation.surface: A gaffe printed in a tabloid, with a woman being taken down a peg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder in print but is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunflower is a tall plant famed for its big yellow flower heads, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: What law's Tom broken somewhere in London?

indicators.note: the words are broken up and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about which statute a man named Tom has violated.
explanation.walkthrough: WALTHAMSTOW is a district of north-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Walthamstow is a part of the borough of Waltham Forest in London.

clue.text: Hot spot encountered in driving lesson

indicators.note: the answer is met with inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A dangerous junction or tricky moment met with while learning to drive.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fireside or chimney corner, literally a warm place by the fire.

clue.text: Great fear about atmosphere around country? Here's method for solving problem

indicators.note: the word for great fear goes round the other pieces

parts.note: terror is extreme fear

indicators.note: the word for atmosphere is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: air is the atmosphere around us
land can mean a country or nation

explanation.surface: Global anxiety over the climate, then a suggestion for how to fix things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the atmosphere backwards and 'about' wraps the fear round both pieces; the surface sells 'atmosphere around country' as a national mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial and error is the approach of testing attempts repeatedly until one works.

clue.text: What gets exciting about moving into new accommodation?

indicators.note: the word for exciting goes around the other piece

parts.note: rousing means stirring or exciting
eh is an interjection asking what was said

explanation.surface: A question about what makes relocating to a new home thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' looks like the start of a question but is EH; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehousing is the act of giving someone a new home, relocating them to different accommodation.

clue.text: We listen to a nobleman's stories

indicators.note: we hear this phrase spoken, matching another word in pronunciation

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman, giving a count's

explanation.surface: An audience hears an aristocrat's tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are narrative reports or descriptions of events, like tales.

clue.text: Suffer from unrequited love and offer some illumination?

definitions.meaning: to carry a torch for someone is to love them without return
literally, holding a lit torch brings light

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pining for someone who does not return affection; taken literally it means bearing a lamp.

clue.text: Panted with journey finally made

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Breathless at the end of a trip, someone finally got there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panted' looks like breathing hard but means longed, as in panting after something.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant for something is to long for it eagerly, as to yearn is.

clue.text: Organise county in need of redevelopment?

parts.note: to run something is to organise or manage it
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An instruction to manage a region that badly needs rebuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWN is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-down describes buildings or areas that are dilapidated and neglected.

clue.text: Liveliness of religious minister bringing two characters to the fore

indicators.text: bringing two characters to the fore
indicators.note: two letters of the minister's word are shifted to its start

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A cleric's vivacity brings two figures forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is borrowed French for spirit, wit and vivacity.

clue.text: Seaman meeting a king coming to a port

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A sailor runs into a monarch arriving at a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese city with a large harbour on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: A duke with little time for estate business?

parts.note: min is short for minute, a little time

explanation.surface: A busy aristocrat barely has a moment for managing his lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Admin is administration, the routine paperwork of running an estate or office.

clue.text: Yours truly's reusing odd bits of food

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker referring to themself, ME

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters are in a strange, irregular order

explanation.surface: Someone admits to recycling strange leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' seems to describe the bits but signals the anagram of REUSING, giving RINGUES; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringues are small baked confections of whipped egg white and sugar.

clue.text: Propose to get elected, wanting no friend to hang about

indicators.note: the friendless phrase hangs round the word for elected

parts.note: someone lacking a friend has no mate
a candidate who gets elected is in

explanation.surface: Advice on a political run: get voted in, but don't loiter without allies.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put them forward as a candidate.

clue.text: It's more cramped, all right, in seaside venue

indicators.note: the word for all right is placed inside the seaside venue

parts.note: a pier at a British resort often holds a theatre or arcade
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone at a resort reports the venue is tighter, but fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Poky describes a small, confined space, so the comparative means smaller and tighter.

clue.text: Dons went mad away from Oxford?

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters have gone wild and are jumbled

explanation.surface: University tutors lost their minds and left the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons are Oxford teachers, which makes the scene apt; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge a student sent down is expelled, removed from the university.

clue.text: Chivalrous type when it is dark, we hear

indicators.note: says the word is identical in pronunciation to one spelt differently

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: A gallant figure who emerges after sunset, so rumour goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is the medieval mounted warrior whose code was chivalry.
